name: Pecan
desc: A long wrinkly nut, sweet and rich, in a smooth shell.
prose: You are a pecan - a long oval nut, deeply wrinkled and grooved, sitting in a smooth reddish-brown shell. Crack you open and the rich sweet kernel inside is buttery and good, baked into sticky pies or toffee or eaten just as you are. Squirrels bury you for winter. Rich and wrinkled and sweetly oily, you are one of the tastiest nuts of all, the star of a gooey pie and a favourite hoard of every busy squirrel.

lines: A smooth creamy nut curved like a moon,
you reach for a handful first of all -
A young little tree, all slender and new,
it bends in the wind and will one day be tall -
A peanut still wrapped in its crinkly shell,
you crack it open in two;
two little nuts in a wrinkly pod -
A big hard nut with three flat sides,
in a shell so tough to crack;
it sits in the mixed-nut bowl at Christmas -
